subject: ventures/bookkeeping-client-fee-calculator
professional: a CPA or senior bookkeeper running a small outsourced bookkeeping practice who prices monthly retainers. First checks: are hours built from volume x timed minutes per task (the time-based cost-plus method), is software a pass-through, is cleanup priced separately as a one-time fee, does the quote cover the periodic work that is not monthly (quarterly sales tax and payroll filings, year-end close, 1099s), and does the roster's effective hourly net out pass-through costs.

evidence.correctness: Independent Python (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/20d3eb67-43fe-5ab8-a54f-4c717b426b39/scratchpad/bk_indep.py) recomputes the time-based retainer by hand: minutes = txn x min/txn(cleanliness) + accounts x 20 + payroll x 25 + AR/AP x 3 + filings x 45 + 30; minimum = h x rate + software; recommended = minimum x 1.2; walk-away = h x 0.75 x rate + software; cleanup = months x minutes x 1.25 / 60 x rate x 1.2; competitor effective = (fee - software)/h. Shipped example (defaults, cleanup 3, competitor 600): 580 min, 9.67 h, 765.00, 918.00, 583.75, 36.25 h, 3,262.50, 57.93 -- engine identical. README CLI example (420 txn, 4 accts, messy, cleanup 3, competitor 600): 1,140 min, 1,465.00, 1,758.00, 1,108.75, 6,412.50, 29.47 below walk-away -- CLI identical. Fixture roster at a non-default 80 target: Garnet 35.71/h +310, Dunn 37.27 +235, Elm 38.33 +500, Alder 43.68 +345, Birch 70.00 +40, Cedar 76.25 +30, Fir at target; 6 of 7 below, total raise 1,460 -- CLI identical. Inputs: 'abc', '1e3' rejected; fractional 2.17 payroll runs accepted. One silent misread: roster row 'Acme,1,200,9.5' (unquoted thousands comma, no dollar sign, no software column) is read as a $1 fee for 200 hours with $9.50 software and ranked at -$0.04/h; the guard at engine.mjs:191 only fires when the fee starts with '$'. The output is absurd enough to notice, so held at 3.
evidence.completeness: Every README/page feature exercised end to end: price (minimum, recommended, walk-away, by-cleanliness table, cleanup quote, competitor effective hourly and status bands) via CLI and the engine the page imports (index.html:170 imports ./engine.mjs, no copy); roster via file and stdin, with --json and --target; quoted CSV fields; header/comment skipping; 200-client cap; usage counter with opt-out, DNT and GPC (usage.mjs). Guide page worked numbers are all pinned by page.test.mjs against the engine. Sitemap covers both pages; served llms.txt has no placeholder origin (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs). No TODOs or stubs.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/bookkeeping-client-fee-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 29/29 pass, 0.12 s. Seven seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py on engine.mjs: raise including software caught; cleanup buffer dropped caught; software dropped from walk-away caught; competitor effective hourly not netting software caught; competitor 'above-recommended' >= -> > SURVIVED; atTarget threshold 1e-9 -> < 1 dollar SURVIVED; widening the thousands-comma guard to fees without '$' SURVIVED (no test pins a 3-digit fee followed by 3-digit hours, nor the no-dollar comma case). 4 of 7 caught: every core formula is pinned by hand-computed values; band boundaries and the comma guard are not.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (241 lines), cli.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script section, all three test files. Pure engine with one validation table (FIELDS) whose bounds are each tested; page and CLI share the engine; HTML escaping on every interpolated string; storage access guarded against SecurityError. Defects: the roster comma guard is a heuristic keyed on a leading '$' (engine.mjs:191); payroll and sales-tax inputs carry step="1" (index.html:55,57) though fractional per-month values are the only way to enter biweekly payroll or quarterly filings, so the browser flags them invalid while the engine accepts them.
evidence.claims: Checked: README formulas (all match engine.mjs:115-142, 213-216); guide/FAQ worked numbers 9.67 h, 765.00, 918.00, 583.75, 577.50, 1,140.00, 36.25 h, 3,262.50, 57.93, roster 3,195.00, 52.5 h, 56.95, 5 of 7, 1,240.00, 80.57, 35.71, 275.00, 550.00, 20.00 (all reproduce); 'no network call' (grep of index/engine/cli/usage: no fetch, XHR, beacon, http import); 'an unquoted $1,200 is refused' (true for that exact form; the no-dollar form is not refused, see defects); usage events named in README and page match record() calls. PARTIAL: INPUT_NOTES software row, rendered on the page (engine.mjs:43), says software 'is added to the fee after your hours, not marked up', but recommended = minimum x (1 + buffer) marks the $40 software up by $8 on the example; README's own formula line states the code's behaviour. Disclaimer, non-affiliation and not-market-rates language on both pages. No fee survey or market figures claimed anywhere.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a bookkeeper quoting a prospect with ~300 transactions, 3 accounts, monthly payroll, and an existing roster of 7 clients. The quote, walk-away and cleanup numbers come out in one pass and the roster immediately shows which clients to raise and by how much -- a usable first-pass pricing worksheet. Gaps a practitioner hits in the first hour: biweekly payroll (2.17 runs/month) and quarterly sales tax (0.33 filings/month) must be typed as fractions with no hint, and the browser marks them invalid (step=1); year-end close, 1099/W-2 season and quarterly 941s have no place except padding the review minutes.
evidence.domain: Compared against the time-based (cost-plus) retainer method taught in bookkeeping-practice pricing guidance (estimate monthly hours from transaction volume and per-task times, multiply by a target billing rate, pass through software, price catch-up/cleanup separately and up front) and the value-pricing school that argues against hourly build-ups. The tool implements the former faithfully and says so. Departures: (1) no periodic/annual work -- year-end close, 1099 and W-2 prep, quarterly payroll returns -- which a CPA checks first because it is where flat retainers lose money; (2) the buffer is applied to software pass-through, contrary to its own note; (3) cleanup multiplies the current-cleanliness minutes by a slow-down factor, so a 'messy' prospect's catch-up is penalised twice (2 min/txn x 1.25), a defensible but unexplained choice; (4) the walk-away floor is a share of target rate rather than the practice's cost per hour, so 'costs you more than the work is worth' is the user's preference, not a cost floor. (1) is the reason for 2.

defects.what: Roster row 'Acme,1,200,9.5' (unquoted thousands comma without a dollar sign, no software column) is silently read as a $1 fee for 200 hours with $9.50 software; the guard only catches fees written with a leading '$'. The README's 'an unquoted $1,200 is refused rather than read as a $1 fee' is true only for that exact spelling.

No place for periodic work a retainer must amortise (year-end close, 1099/W-2 prep, quarterly payroll returns), and no guidance that biweekly payroll or quarterly sales tax are entered as fractions per month; the page inputs carry step=1, so the browser marks 2.17 or 0.33 invalid.
The page's input note says software 'is added to the fee after your hours, not marked up', but the recommended fee applies the buffer to minimum including software ($918 vs $910 on the example).
Status-band and at-target boundaries untested: competitorFee >= recommended -> > and atTarget threshold 1e-9 -> $1 both survive mutation, as does widening the comma guard.

verdict: A correct, honest time-based retainer calculator. Every recomputed output reproduces exactly by hand: the shipped example (580 min, $765 minimum, $918 quote, $583.75 walk-away, $3,262.50 cleanup, $57.93/h at the competitor fee), the README's messy-books CLI example ($1,465 / $1,758 / $1,108.75 / $6,412.50) and the fixture roster at an untested $80 target (6 of 7 below, +$1,460). Tests pass 29/29 and catch every seeded formula change but none of three boundary mutants. It meets the bar on the gates; domain falls short because a CPA's first question, where year-end, 1099 and quarterly work goes, has no answer beyond padding the review minutes. Smaller defects: an unquoted '1,200' fee without a dollar sign is silently read as $1, and the page says software is not marked up while the recommended fee buffers it.
